headline: Public docs teardown: highest-impact fixes and the automation layer to prioritize first

summary.executive_summary: Modal.com documentation comprises 1,049 crawled pages with 100% crawl coverage across 1,091 discovered URLs. Critical issues include 38 confirmed broken internal documentation links, 10.81% API reference coverage across 213 detected API pages, and only 24.69% of pages displaying last-updated timestamps. Retrieval readiness scores 77.68/100 (moderate band) with 70.47% of content flagged as stale-risk due to missing freshness signals. Evidence coverage stands at 72.72% (1,410 of 1,939 key claims supported), while actionability reaches 90%.

key_findings.headline: Undocumented API operations
key_findings.business_consequence: Generate/update reference + how-to from OpenAPI and enforce drift checks.

key_findings.headline: Documentation freshness debt
key_findings.business_consequence: Prioritize stale pages via weekly SLA loop and lifecycle policies.

key_findings.headline: Code/docs contract drift
key_findings.business_consequence: Track interface changes and enforce docs updates with report-first governance.

priority_actions.title: Fix all 38 confirmed broken internal documentation links
priority_actions.why_this_first: Broken links directly block user workflows and erode trust; fixing 38 links is low-effort with immediate navigation and support-ticket reduction payoff.

priority_actions.title: Add last-updated timestamps to the 75.31% of pages missing freshness metadata
priority_actions.why_this_first: Surfacing freshness on 790+ pages reduces stale-risk from 70.47% and boosts user confidence, SEO ranking, and LLM retrieval quality with minimal engineering lift.

priority_actions.title: Expand API usage documentation to cover the 89% gap across 213 detected API pages
priority_actions.why_this_first: API coverage at 10.81% is a major onboarding and adoption blocker; closing this gap drives developer success, reduces support load, and accelerates time-to-value.

strengths: 100% crawl coverage with 1,049 pages successfully indexed from 1,091 discovered URLs
Zero repository navigation broken links; all 38 broken links are user-facing documentation paths
90% actionability coverage indicates strong task-oriented content
risks: 38 confirmed broken internal documentation links degrade user trust and navigation flow
10.81% API reference coverage leaves 89% of 213 detected API pages without usage documentation
70.47% stale-risk content due to missing last-updated metadata on 75.31% of pages
72.72% evidence coverage means 529 key claims lack supporting examples, links, or code snippets
limitations: External audit cannot verify content technical accuracy, correctness of code examples, or alignment with current product behavior.
Link verification excluded 2 URLs due to authentication, rate-limiting, or server blocks; actual broken-link count may differ if these require credentials.
Freshness and staleness metrics rely on visible last-updated metadata; pages may be current but lack timestamps, inflating stale-risk estimates.
automation_first: Deploy automated broken-link scanning on every commit or daily schedule to catch and alert on internal link rot before users encounter 404s; fixing the current 38 broken links manually is urgent, but preventing recurrence saves ongoing support and trust costs.

Implement Git-based last-commit timestamp injection into page metadata for the 75.31% of pages missing freshness signals; this one-time pipeline change eliminates 70.47% stale-risk flagging and continuously maintains user confidence and SEO freshness without manual updates.

Build automated API reference cross-check between code annotations and published docs to flag the 89% coverage gap across 213 API pages; continuous validation ensures new API surfaces are documented at release, reducing onboarding friction and support escalations.
